author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through a form prefilled with its current values. The correction is validated like a booking and changes that visit in place, adding no visit to the pet.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a new description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries them and the owner's record is shown
given a booked visit, when a correction is submitted, then the pet has the same number of visits as before
given a booked visit, when a blank description is submitted, then the correction is refused, the form is shown again, and the description is named
given a booked visit, when a date of today or earlier is submitted, then the correction is refused, the form is shown again, and the date is named
edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not exist, or that does not belong to the named pet, is refused
non_goals: an edit link or any other visible entry point on the owner's record (owner decision: reachable by URL alone in this request)
changing which pet a visit belongs to
any rule for past visits other than the booking rule (open question in docs/prd.md)
notes: Owner-quoted mechanism constraints live in intake line 1 and are for system-design-expert: the GET/POST route /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, reuse of the template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its `visit` model attribute, and a redirect to the owner detail page on success. Narrowest readings taken where the intake was silent: edge case 3 refuses an unknown or mismatched visit, following Visits edge case 1 and Owner records edge case 2; edge case 4 applies the future-date rule to a correction even when the visit is already past, and the PRD records this as an open question. NG-5 narrowing recorded in docs/adr/2026-10-25-non-goal-visit-cancellation-only.md; the 2026-08-08 ADR status line now points to it. docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new ADR; that file is outside this agent's write scope, so system-design-expert or root adds it.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction extends the existing visit workflow in VisitController (system-design § Contracts: VisitController, Visit, Pet, Owner, OwnerRepository rows now carry REQ-VIS-003). It stays inside the owner aggregate: owner -> pet -> visit, written only through OwnerRepository cascade (§ Contracts, Invariants paragraph). Two adjustments make it minor rather than covered. (1) The class-level @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit always constructs a new Visit and adds it to the pet, so an edit routed through it unchanged would give the pet an extra visit on save. The method branches instead: when the route carries a visitId it resolves the existing visit through the pet (new Pet lookup by identity, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer)) and adds nothing; the booking branch keeps its current behavior. (2) The future-date rule now has two entry points, so it moves out of the controller onto Visit (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row and the note that a new controller rule is a fresh violation): Visit answers whether its date is later than a supplied today (a clock-free argument keeps the entity free of I/O). Booking and correction both call it and translate a refusal into the existing typeMismatch.visitDate field error. Booking's observable behavior is unchanged. New § Scale and Load row covers the visit lookup. Grep-based basis (no IDE oracle connected): VisitController.java:62-81 builds and attaches the new Visit; Owner.java:126 getPet(Integer) is the lookup pattern; BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode, so mutating a visit held in Pet's LinkedHashSet is safe.
integration_points: Routes: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit on VisitController. GET renders pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with the resolved visit as the `visit` model attribute. POST validates (@Valid for @NotBlank description, plus the Visit date rule), redisplays the same view on errors, and on success saves the owner and redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} (owner-quoted mechanism, intake line 1).

Binding target (POST edit): the persisted Visit resolved from owner -> pet -> visitId, behind an allow-list of date and description on the `visit` binder, and keeping the existing id/*.id disallow list (security-principles § Mass assignment). The create form offers only those two fields, so applying the allow-list to the shared `visit` binder leaves booking unchanged. The Owner taken from the model is not request-bound on the edit handler (e.g. @ModelAttribute(binding = false)).

Refusal (edge case 3): an unknown visitId, or one the named pet does not hold, is refused through the same mechanism as an unknown owner or pet in loadPetWithVisit, an IllegalArgumentException flowing outward to the error page (architecture-principles § error flow). The message names identifiers only (security-principles § Secret disclosure). Each request re-resolves owner, pet and visit (security-principles § Trusting cross-request state).

Double for OwnerRepository: the existing @MockitoBean stub in VisitControllerTests (a @WebMvcTest slice with no JPA). The stub only returns a fixture Owner graph, and the tests assert on that graph's state: the edited visit's date and description, and the pet's visit count unchanged. Interaction verification stays minimal. Reason a real implementation or hand-written double does not fit: the slice has no JPA context, and a hand-written double of the JpaRepository surface is disproportionate to one findById/save pair (testing-principles mocking policy; Mockito tolerated).
Double for the HTTP transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned framework stub (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).
Visit date rule: covered by a plain unit test (VisitTests) with no Spring context and an explicit today argument, below the controller tests (testing-principles § Test Pyramid).

risks.risk: A second copy of the future-date check in the edit handler would be a new controller business rule.
risks.mitigation: Visit owns the rule; both handlers delegate to it and only map the result to a field error (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row).

risks.risk: A failed correction leaves a half-applied write.
risks.mitigation: On validation failure the handler returns the form without calling save. The owner graph is request-local, since open-in-view is disabled and each request reloads it, so nothing persists (architecture-principles § Fail secure).

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: No test asserts that a successful correction saves the owner. The success test compares the mutated fixture graph, which the binder changes whether or not the handler calls owners.save(owner); with OwnerRepository a @MockitoBean, deleting `this.owners.save(owner)` from processVisitCorrectionForm leaves every test green, while in production (open-in-view disabled) the correction would never persist. The refusal tests verify never().save, but nothing verifies the positive save. Here the interaction is the contract, since the repository save is the only persistence path (system-design Invariants: persisted only through Owner cascade). Change caught: removal of the save call.
findings.fix: In the success test (or a sibling theVisitCorrectionShouldBeSaved test) add then(this.owners).should().save(owner) against the fixture owner, so the owner is held in a field or the captured argument is compared whole.

findings.description: Pet.getVisit(Integer) is a new domain lookup that the design places on Pet (mirroring Owner.getPet), below the controller boundary. It has two decision paths (match by id, skip of new/unsaved visits, null when absent) and is tested only through the @WebMvcTest slice, one path (match, plus not-found via the other pet's visit id). The isNew skip and the null-for-absent result have no unit test at the Pet seam (grep -F -e 'getVisit(' src/test returns no hit). Change caught: dropping the `!visit.isNew()` guard would let a null id match a freshly attached booking visit.
findings.fix: Add a plain unit test class PetTests (no Spring context) covering: returns the visit with the given id, returns null for an id the pet does not hold, and does not return an unsaved visit. Keep the controller test as the one representative path.

findings.description: The two mass-assignment controls this slice adds (allow-list of date and description on the visit binder, binding=false on the Owner) have no test. A POST to the correction route carrying `id`, `pet.id`, or owner fields such as `owner.firstName` is never exercised; removing either control leaves all six new tests green. security-principles § Mass assignment is the stated rationale in the design-block. Change caught: removal or widening of the allow-list or binding=false.
findings.fix: Add one test posting a valid date/description plus an extra `id` and an owner field param, then assert with the whole-object comparison that the visit id and the owner are unchanged.

findings.description: Edge case 3 (coverage-map: correcting a visit that does not exist or does not belong to the named pet is refused) is tested for one half only. The assertion is hasCauseInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class) with no message check, so it would also pass if the owner or pet lookup threw. An unknown visitId is not exercised; the shared null path makes it one equivalence class, but the weak assertion does not pin that the refusal comes from the visit lookup nor that identifiers only appear in the message.
findings.fix: Assert the cause message names the visit and pet ids (e.g. hasRootCauseMessage with the expected 'Visit with id ... not found for pet with id ...' text built from the named constants) and add no second case.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Ownership chain re-resolved per request (security-principles § Trusting cross-request state): VisitController.java:95-96 `if (visitId == null) { return attachNewVisit(pet); }` / `return findVisitOfPet(pet, visitId);` resolves the visit only from the owner-loaded pet's own visits (Pet.java getVisit iterates `getVisits()`), so a visitId from another pet or owner is refused with IllegalArgumentException; VisitControllerTests.java:199 `theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitDoesNotBelongToThePet` exercises it

Mass assignment: the new `@InitBinder("visit")` at VisitController.java:61 `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");` stacks on the retained global `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");` (line 53), strengthening the booking route too; the correction POST binds Owner with `@ModelAttribute(binding = false) Owner owner` (line 151), so the hidden `petId` and any owner fields in the body never bind

Validation holds on the new persisting path: correction handler carries `@Valid Visit visit` (Visit.description is `@NotBlank`) plus the shared `rejectDateOnOrBeforeToday`, and saves only when `result.hasErrors()` is false; the moved booking check is equivalent (`this.date != null && !this.date.isAfter(today)` vs. the removed `visit.getDate() != null && !visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now())`), so no check was weakened
No dirty-flush bypass of validation on the error path: application.properties `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false`, so the bound-but-rejected managed Visit is never flushed

Error text carries only integer path ids (`"Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + pet.getId()`), no sensitive values reaching the error page; visitId is typed Integer, so non-numeric input fails conversion before use

Output escaping: the reused createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders date/description via `th:text` and the form fragments (no `th:utext`, no `__${...}__` preprocessing in the template as read); no query construction added — persistence goes through `owners.save(owner)`

New surface stated: GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, unauthenticated like every other route per the demonstration baseline in system-design.md § Security Context; no actuator or exposure change

Supply chain: no build.gradle/pom.xml change in this diff (`git diff --stat -- build.gradle pom.xml` empty); OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -n -i 'dependencyCheck\|owasp' build.gradle` empty), so no NVD match ran; resolved runtimeClasspath shows spring-boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final

author: change-grader
summary: add correction of a booked visit's date and description

blast_radius.note: The code stays in one package (owner), but it adds a new unauthenticated write route, and every visit request now runs through the changed class-level @ModelAttribute loadPetWithVisit. The new @InitBinder("visit") allow-list also applies to the existing booking route. On top of that, five docs change, including narrowing a confirmed non-goal (NG-5).

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks turned up no hidden behavior change. The moved booking date check is equivalent to the inline one it replaces (date != null && !date.isAfter(today)). The allow-list changes nothing observable on booking because Visit binds only date and description. The visitId branch attaches nothing on correction. Pet.getVisit skips unsaved visits, so a null id cannot match the new-visit placeholder. Two oddities are visible: the reused form still labels its button Add Visit, and a past-dated visit cannot be corrected without moving its date. The second is documented as PRD edge case 4 and recorded as an open question.

test_adequacy.note: The tests check real outcomes. The visit is compared field by field after correction, the owner save is verified, the pet's visit count is pinned, posted id and firstName values are ignored, the today boundary is refused with no save, and a foreign visit id is refused with the exact message. PetTests and VisitTests cover the new domain methods at their boundaries. The only gap is that no test fails if just the visit allow-list is removed, which the test reviewer called defence in depth.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved on round 2 after round 1's test-reviewer changes_requested was fixed in a tests-only delta. However, the late-round code-quality approval carries recommendations forward: Javadoc tags, the 'booking' wording that ubiquitous-language lists as Avoid, and the isDatedOnOrBefore Javadoc stating the inverse of what the method returns. The doc-reviewer did not verify the reused template or the message bundle.

scope_deviation.note: No design revisions, consultations, or build retries. The diff adds exactly the GET/POST edit pair, no edit link, and no cancel path, matching the intake decisions. The fix-round delta touched tests only.

rationale: The change is contained and its logic holds on reading, and the tests are substantive.
